questions.excerpt: A dice is thrown twice. What is the probability that the sum of outcomes is a prime number?$3 / 36$ $19 / 36$ $15 / 36$ $13 / 36$
questions.questionText: A dice is thrown twice. What is the probability that the sum of outcomes is a prime number? $3 / 36$ $19 / 36$ $15 / 36$ $13 / 36$
questions.questionHtml:
A dice is thrown twice. What is the probability that the sum of outcomes is a prime number?

  1. $3 / 36$
     
  2. $19 / 36$
     
  3. $15 / 36$
     
  4. $13 / 36$
questions.explanation: 1. Find the Total Number of Outcomes A standard die has 6 faces {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\} When a die is thrown twice, the total number of possible outcomes is: {Total Outcomes} = 6 * 6 = 36 2. Identify Possible Prime Sums The minimum sum possible is 1 + 1 = 2 The maximum sum possible is 6 + 6 = 12. The prime numbers between 2 and 12 are: 2, 3, 5, 7, and 11 . 3. Count the Favorable Outcomes Now, we list the pairs (x, y) from each throw that add up to these prime numbers: Sum = 2: (1, 1) — 1 outcome Sum = 3: (1, 2), (2, 1)$ — 2 outcomes Sum = 5: (1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 1)$ — 4 outcomes Sum = 7: (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 4), (4, 3), (5, 2), (6, 1) — 6 outcomes Sum = 11: (5, 6), (6, 5) — 2 outcomes Total Favorable Outcomes  = 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15$ 4. Calculate the Probability The probability (P) is the ratio of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes: P = \frac{\text{Favorable Outcomes}}/{{Total Outcomes}} P = 15/36 akash_kumar 9 answered Feb 13 akash_kumar 9 comm

questions.questionText: A day can be either cloudy or sunny. The probability of a day being cloudy is $0.5$, independent of the condition of other days, then find the probability for any given $4$ days such that it will be $3$ cloudy days and $1$ sunny day. $1 / 4$ $2 / 3$ $3 / 4$ $3 / 8$
questions.questionHtml:
A day can be either cloudy or sunny. The probability of a day being cloudy is $0.5$, independent of the condition of other days, then find the probability for any given $4$ days such that it will be $3$ cloudy days and $1$ sunny day.

  1. $1 / 4$
     
  2. $2 / 3$
     
  3. $3 / 4$
     
  4. $3 / 8$
questions.explanation: Each day can be Cloudy (C) or Sunny (S) with probability 0.5, and days are independent. Total days = 4 P(Cloudy) = 0.5 P(Sunny) = 0.5 We need the probability of exactly 3 cloudy days and 1 sunny day. Number of ways to choose 3 cloudy days out of 4: 4C3 = 4 Probability of any one specific arrangement (e.g., CCCS): (0.5)^3 × (0.5)^1 = (0.5)^4 = 1/16 Since there are 4 such arrangements, Required probability = 4 × (1/16) = 4/16 = 1/4 Final Answer: 1/4 Mehakpreet_Singh 1 answered Feb 14 Mehakpreet_Singh 1 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.questionText: A boat can cover a distance of $7.2$ km downstream and $3.2$ km upstream in $2$ hours. It can also cover $1.5$ km downstream and $0.6$ km upstream in $24$ minutes. What is the speed of the boat when going downstream (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$) ? $6$ $4.5$ $5$ $7.5$
questions.questionHtml:
A boat can cover a distance of $7.2$ km downstream and $3.2$ km upstream in $2$ hours. It can also cover $1.5$ km downstream and $0.6$ km upstream in $24$ minutes. What is the speed of the boat when going downstream (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$) ?

  1. $6$
     
  2. $4.5$
     
  3. $5$
     
  4. $7.5$
questions.explanation: Upstream speed $=u \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$   Downstream speed $=\mathrm{dkm} / \mathrm{h}$   According to the question \begin{equation*} \frac{7.2}{d}+\frac{3.2}{u}=2 \tag{1} \end{equation*} And \begin{equation*} \frac{1.5}{d}+\frac{0.6}{u}=\frac{24}{60}=\frac{2}{5} \tag{2} \end{equation*} Multiply equation (1) by $5$ and eq (2) by $2.4$ and subtract eq (2) from (1) $\left(\frac{36}{d}+\frac{16}{u}\right)-\left(\frac{36}{d}+\frac{14.4}{u}\right)=10-\frac{48}{5}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{1.6}{u}=\frac{2}{5}$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=4 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ Put this value in either of the example For example $\frac{7.2}{d}+\frac{3.2}{u}=2 \Rightarrow \frac{7.2}{d}+\frac{3.2}{4}=2$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{d}=6 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ GO Classes answered Feb 1 GO Classes comment Share Follow See all 5 Comments 5 5 Comments reply Show 2 previous comments gauravsurana628 commented Feb 1 reply Follow flag @GO Classes  The answer key must be updated for 2 aptitude questions. 0

questions.questionText: Prof. Murphy likes to let her students choose who their partners will be; however, no pair of students may work together for more than seven class periods in a row. Alice and Bob have worked together for seven class periods in a row. Calvin and Denny have worked together for three class periods in a row. Calvin does not want to work with Alice. Who should be assigned to work with Bob? Calvin Alice Denny None
questions.questionHtml:
Prof. Murphy likes to let her students choose who their partners will be; however, no pair of students may work together for more than seven class periods in a row.

Alice and Bob have worked together for seven class periods in a row. Calvin and Denny have worked together for three class periods in a row. Calvin does not want to work with Alice.

Who should be assigned to work with Bob?

  1. Calvin
     
  2. Alice
     
  3. Denny
     
  4. None
questions.explanation: The rule states that no pair of students may work together for more than seven class periods in a row. Alice and Bob have already worked together for seven consecutive class periods. Therefore, assigning Alice to Bob again would violate the rule. Calvin does not want to work with Alice, but this restriction does not involve Bob, so it does not prevent Calvin from working with Bob. There is no restriction given that prevents Denny from working with Bob either. Hence, assigning Alice to Bob is not allowed, while assigning Calvin or Denny to Bob is allowed. Since a valid assignment exists, the option “None” is incorrect. Among the given choices, Calvin is a correct assignment.

questions.questionHtml:
Amar, Akbar and Anthony are three friends, one of whom is a doctor, another is an engineer and the third is a professor. Amar is not an engineer. Akbar is the shortest. The tallest person is a doctor. The engineer's height is the geometric mean of the heights of the other two. Then which of the following is true?

  1. Amar is a doctor and he is the tallest
     
  2. Akbar is a professor and he is the tallest
     
  3. Anthony is an engineer and he is shortest
     
  4. Anthony is a doctor and he is the tallest

options.label: A
options.text: Amar is a doctor and he is the tallest

options.label: B
options.text: Akbar is a professor and he is the tallest

options.label: C
options.text: Anthony is an engineer and he is shortest

options.label: D
options.text: Anthony is a doctor and he is the tallest

questions.explanation: The engineers height is the geometric mean of the other two $\Rightarrow$ the engineer is neither tallest nor shortest (he is the middle height). Tallest person is a doctor  doctor $\neq$ engineer. Akbar is the shortest $\Rightarrow$ Akbar is not the engineer and not the doctor. Therefore, Akbar is the professor. Amar is not an engineer (given). Since Akbar and Amar are not engineers, Anthony must be the engineer (middle height). The remaining profession (doctor) goes to Amar, and since the doctor is tallest: Amar is the doctor and he is the tallest. Hence, Option A is true. questions.questionHtml:
Talking to his wife over the telephone after their home was burgled, the husband said "Niether of the dogs $\_\_\_\_\_$ hurt, nor $\_\_\_\_\_$ any of the jewels stolen." Which of the following options is technically the most correct choice of verbs for the above blanks, in the order they would appear in the sentence above?

  1. was, was
     
  2. was, were
     
  3. were, was
     
  4. were, were

questions.questionText: Ms. Carroll promised that anyone who got all the multiple choice questions right on the upcoming exam would receive an $A$ on the exam. Which one of these statements necessarily follows logically? If Lewis did not receive an A , then he got all of the multiple choice questions wrong. If Lewis did not receive an A, then he got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong. If Lewis got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong, then he did not receive an A. If Lewis received an A, then he got all of the multiple choice questions right.
questions.questionHtml:
Ms. Carroll promised that anyone who got all the multiple choice questions right on the upcoming exam would receive an $A$ on the exam. Which one of these statements necessarily follows logically?

  1. If Lewis did not receive an A , then he got all of the multiple choice questions wrong.
     
  2. If Lewis did not receive an A, then he got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong.
     
  3. If Lewis got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong, then he did not receive an A.
     
  4. If Lewis received an A, then he got all of the multiple choice questions right.

options.label: A
options.text: If Lewis did not receive an A , then he got all of the multiple choice questions wrong.

options.label: B
options.text: If Lewis did not receive an A, then he got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong.

options.label: C
options.text: If Lewis got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong, then he did not receive an A.

options.label: D
options.text: If Lewis received an A, then he got all of the multiple choice questions right.

questions.explanation: The given promise can be expressed in logical form as follows: Let \(P\) denote the statement “Lewis got all the multiple-choice questions right” and let \(Q\) denote the statement “Lewis received an A.” The promise made by Ms. Carroll is: \( P \Rightarrow Q \) A statement is always logically equivalent to its contrapositive. The contrapositive of \( P \Rightarrow Q \) is: \( \neg Q \Rightarrow \neg P \) Contrapositive is:  If Lewis did not receive an A, then he did not get all the multiple-choice questions right. If Lewis did not receive an A, then he got at least one of the multiple-choice questions wrong. Therefore, the correct answer is B .

questions.questionText: Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow: Odisha has colourful fairs and festivals and are as numerous as the days of the year. The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple to the divine shrine called the Gundicha Temple is known as the Car Festival or the Rath Yatra. On this occasion, the deities adorn three chariots named Nandigosha, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana respectively. They stay in the divine shrine for nine days and then return to the Jagannath Temple. This journey is called Bahuda Jatra. This grand festival of Odisha is visited by lakhs of devotees from India and abroad who pull the sacred chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple and back on a broad road called Badadanda. The festival begins from the second day of Shukla Paksha (bright half) in the month of Ashadha (June-July) every year. This festival of Lord Jagannath, who is worshipped as the Lord of the Universe, is celebrated not only in Puri, but also in many other places in India and abroad. Whereas the festival of Lord Jagannath is celebrated in many places in India and abroad, it is primarily associated with which city? Bhuvaneswar Puri Cuttack Konark

The festival begins from the second day of Shukla Paksha (bright half) in the month of Ashadha (June-July) every year. questions.explanation: Amiable: This is an adjective meaning friendly and pleasant. It is the most common way to describe a manager's temperament in a professional yet positive light. Ambiguous: This means open to more than one interpretation or having a double meaning. While a manager could be ambiguous, it usually describes a statement or a situation rather than a "nature." Animosity: This is a noun meaning strong hostility. Since the sentence requires an adjective to describe "nature," this is grammatically incorrect. Hostile: This is an adjective meaning unfriendly or antagonistic. While grammatically correct, it is less common in general descriptions unless specifically highlighting a conflict. so option D is correct

questions.excerpt: The sequence $S$ is defined by $S_{n}=S_{n-1}+S_{n-2}-1$ for each integer $n \geq 3$. If $S_{1}=11$ and $S_{3}=10$, what is the value of $S_{5}$ ?091018
questions.questionText: The sequence $S$ is defined by $S_{n}=S_{n-1}+S_{n-2}-1$ for each integer $n \geq 3$. If $S_{1}=11$ and $S_{3}=10$, what is the value of $S_{5}$ ? 0 9 10 18
questions.questionHtml:
The sequence $S$ is defined by $S_{n}=S_{n-1}+S_{n-2}-1$ for each integer $n \geq 3$. If $S_{1}=11$ and $S_{3}=10$, what is the value of $S_{5}$ ?

  1. 0
  2. 9
  3. 10
  4. 18
questions.explanation: (D). The sequence $S_{n}=S_{n-1}+S_{n-2}-1$ can be read as "to get any term in sequence $S$, sum the two previous terms and subtract 1 ." The problem gives the first term and the third term and asks for the fifth term: $$ \frac{11}{S_{1}} \quad \frac{}{S_{2}} \quad \frac{10}{S_{3}} \quad \frac{}{S_{4}} \quad \frac{}{S_{5}} $$ Within the sequence $S_{1}$ to $S_{3}$, the problem gives two values but not the middle one $\left(S_{2}\right)$. What version of the formula would include those three terms? $$ \begin{aligned} S_{3} & =S_{2}+S_{1}-1 \\ 10 & =S_{2}+(11)-1 \\ 10 & =S_{2}+10 \\ 0 & =S_{2} \end{aligned} $$ $$ \frac{11}{S_{1}} \quad \frac{0}{S_{2}} \quad \frac{10}{S_{3}} \quad \frac{}{S_{4}} \quad \frac{}{S_{5}} $$ To get each subsequent term, sum the two previous terms and subtract 1 . Thus, $S_{4}=10+0-1=9$ and $S_{5}=9+10-1=18$ : $$ \frac{11}{S_{1}} \quad \frac{0}{S_{2}} \quad \frac{10}{S_{3}} \quad \frac{9}{S_{4}} \quad \frac{18}{S_{5}} $$ GO Classes ans

  2. $\frac{1}{8}$
  3. $\frac{5}{9}$

questions.explanation: (A). Let P's age when she got married $=x$ years According to question, Present age of $\mathrm{P}=\frac{8}{5} \times x$---(i) Since, it is given that she got married 15 years ago Present age of $\mathrm{P}=x+15----$ (ii) Equate equation (i) and (ii) we get; $\frac{8}{5} x=x+15$ $8 x=5 x+75$ $3 x=75 \Rightarrow x=25$ year So, present age of $P(x+15)=40$ year Now, present age of her son$=40 \times \frac{1}{5}=8$ year Hence, required fraction $=\frac{8-4}{40-4}=\frac{4}{36}=\frac{1}{9}$ GO Classes answered Jun 13, 2025 GO Classes comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.questionHtml:
In the figure below $W X Y Z$ is a rectangle with $W X=4$ and $W Z=8$. Point $M$ lies $\overline{X Y}$, point $A$ lies on $\overline{Y Z}$, and $\angle W M A$ is a right angle. The areas of $\triangle W X M$ and $\triangle W A Z$ are equal. What is the area of $\triangle W M A$ ?


Note: On certain tests that took place in China, the problem asked for the area of $\triangle M A Y$.

  1. 13
  2. 14
  3. 15
  4. 16
questions.explanation: We know that $W X=4, W Z=8$, so $Y Z=4$ and $Y X=8$. Since $\angle W M A=90^{\circ}$, triangles $W X M$ and $M Y A$ are similar. Therefore, $\frac{W X}{M Y}=\frac{X M}{Y A}$, which gives $\frac{4}{8-X M}=\frac{X M}{4-Z A}$. We also know that the areas of triangles $W X M$ and $W A Z$ are equal, so $W X \cdot X M=W Z \cdot Z A$, which implies $4 \cdot X M=8 \cdot Z A$. Substituting this into the previous equation, we get $\frac{4}{8-2 Z A}=\frac{X M}{4-Z A}$, yielding $Z A=1$ and $X M=2$. Thus, $$ \triangle W M A=4 \cdot 8-\frac{4 \cdot 2}{2}-\frac{8 \cdot 1}{2}-\frac{6 \cdot 3}{2}=(\mathbf{C}) 15 $$ GO Classes answered Jun 13, 2025 GO Classes comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.explanation: Use a system of equations. Let $x$ be the weight of a pizza and $y$ be the weight of a cup of orange slices. Multiply both sides by $x$ to get $x^{2}+1=x \sqrt{5}$ Squaring both sides: $$ x^{4}+2 x^{2}+1=5 x^{2} $$ Subtract $2 x^{2}$ from both sides: $$ x^{4}+1=3 x^{2} $$ Squaring both sides: $$ x^{8}+2 x^{4}+1=9 x^{4} $$ Subtract $9 x^{4}$ from both sides: $$ x^{8}-7 x^{4}+1=0 $$ Multiply $x^{3}$ on both sides: $$ x^{11}-7 x^{7}+x^{3}=(\mathrm{B}) 0 $$ GO Classes answered Jun 13, 2025 GO Classes comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.questionText: A box contains five cards, numbered $1,2,3,4$, and 5 . Three cards are selected randomly without replacement from the box. What is the probability that 4 is the largest value selected? $\frac{1}{10}$ $\frac{1}{5}$ $\frac{3}{10}$ $\frac{2}{5}$

A box contains five cards, numbered $1,2,3,4$, and 5 . Three cards are selected randomly without replacement from the box. What is the probability that 4 is the largest value selected?

  1. $\frac{1}{10}$
     
  2. $\frac{1}{5}$
     
  3. $\frac{3}{10}$
     
  4. $\frac{2}{5}$
questions.explanation: (C). There are $\binom{5}{3}$ possible groups of cards that can be selected. If 4 is the largest card selected, then the other two cards must be either 1,2 , or 3 , for a total $\binom{3}{2}$ groups of cards. Then, the probability is just $\frac{\binom{3}{2}}{\binom{5}{3}}=(\mathbf{C}) \frac{3}{10}$.

Let the amount invested at one part $=x$ According to the question $\frac{x \times \frac{20}{3} \times \frac{21}{5}}{100}=\quad 2 \times$ $(5000-x) \times 4 \times \frac{11}{4}$ $420 \mathrm{x}=1650000-330 \mathrm{x}$ $750 \mathrm{x}=1650000$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2200$ Amount invested in the second part $=$ $5000-2200=2800$ Desired difference $=2800-2200=600$ GO Classes answered Jun 17, 2025 2 flags: ✌ Edit necessary (Sarvi Agarwal “please recheck, i think this solution is wrong”) ✌ Edit necessary (balaji2409 “percentage conversion is wrong in RHS”) GO Classes comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. 0 0 votes $\frac{x\times \frac{20}{3}\times \frac{21}{5}}{100} = \frac{(5000-x)\times4 \times\frac{11}{4}}{100}\times 2$ $\implies x = \frac{5000\times11}{25} = 2200$ Difference in split values is   $5000-x - x = 5000 - 2x = 5000 - 4400 = 600$ $\therefore \textbf{Opion B}$ is correct.

questions.explanation: (B). Since there are 557 households, the median household would be midway between the 1st and 557th households on the list if the households are ranked by how many pets they own. The midpoint between the 1st and 557th households is the $\frac{(1+557)}{2}=279$ th household. Check: There are 278 households below this one, and 278 households above (because $279+278=$ 557). Ranked by number of pets, households 1 through 70 (the first 70 households) have one pet, which means households 71 through 316 (in other words, the next 246 households) have two pets. Since the 279th household falls in this interval, the median household owns two pets. questions.explanation: The correct answer is like good The objective is to identify the segment containing an error. Examining the sentence segments: 1. In this cold wheather 2. there's nothing 3 like good 4. cup of coffee The segment "like good" is incorrect because it lacks an article before the adjective-noun combination. The correct phrase should be "like a good," making "in this cold weather, there's nothing like a good cup of coffee."

  1. Voluntary
  2. Obligatory
  3. Compliantly
  4. Overtly
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Voluntary The task is to identify the antonym of the underlined word compulsory in the sentence: "The CEO called for compulsory participation from each employee." The word compulsory means required or mandatory. We are given four options: Voluntary Obligatory Compliantly Overtly The word that best signifies the opposite of compulsory is voluntary, which means participation done by choice without being mandatory. Thus, the most appropriate antonym of the word compulsory is Voluntary.

___________________ he not called you in advance, you would have been late.
 

  1. If
  2. Were
  3. Had
  4. Could
questions.explanation: The word "Had" is correct in this sentence because it introduces a third conditional sentence in its inverted form. Third conditional sentences are used to describe hypothetical situations in the past—things that did not actually happen. A typical third conditional sentence uses the following structure: If + past perfect tense, would have + past participle In this sentence, the past perfect tense ("had not called") is necessary because we are talking about a past situation that could have been different. "Had" introduces the past perfect tense needed for a third conditional.  It conveys that the situation (him calling) happened before another past event (you arriving on time), which is why you weren’t late. Option A is not correct: If : While "If" works with conditional sentences, it doesn't fit here because it doesn't align with the inverted sentence structure.   Option B is not correct: Were: "Were" is used for se

questions.questionHtml:
A computer is programmed to generate $n$ natural numbers, each lesser than $1000$ at random.It displays the sum of the digits of each generated number.


Statement:
One can definitely find five numbers among the $n$ displayed results whose values are the same.
The smallest possible value of $n$ is _________  that makes the above statement always TRUE.

Note: Random means there is no specific choice!
questions.explanation: Using the pigeonhole principle : There are 28 possible sums.  How? [ A natural number x < 1000 can be written as x = 100a + 10b + c, where a,b,c are the digits of x.  The sum of the digits is S(x) = a + b + c.  Range of possible sums : Minimum sum: 0+0+1. (Any of the digits 1) Maximum sum: 9+9+9=27. Thus, the possible values of S(x) are integers from 1 to 27, inclusive. There are 27 distinct possible sums .  ] To guarantee that at least 5 numbers have the same sum: First, assign 4 numbers to each sum (this fills 4 × 27 = 108 numbers without any sum appearing 5 times). The 109th number will force one sum to appear 5 times. Thus, the smallest n is 109 . (Assuminig Natural number starting from 1 and not 0, if starts from 0, then we will have 28 distinct sums, leading to 28 x 4 + 1 = 113) GAURAV_JHA answered Jan 7, 2025 GAURAV_JHA comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. This is likely the opening sentence — it sets up the theme. S  gives a specific incident:  One day, when a bull gave him chase, Shifu began running for his life. This follows naturally after the general statement — a story illustrating the idea. P  shows the student’s question:  Shifu’s student exclaimed, “Why do you run since the bull is an illusion?” This happens after Shifu runs — the student questions the action given the earlier proclamation. Q  is Shifu’s reply:  Shifu said, “Surely my running away from the bull is also an illusion.” This is the punchline — answering the student’s question. So the order is:  R → S → P → Q  (RSPQ). questions.questionHtml:
Direction $(56 - 60 )$: Complete the sentences using most appropriate options given below :

The  ________ of the mountains stood out as craggy________ on the horizon.

  1. Colors; shapes
  2. Shapes; textures
  3. Outline; shapes
  4. Textures; lines
questions.explanation: The most appropriate option is: C. Outline ; shapes Complete sentence: The outline of the mountains stood out as craggy shapes on the horizon. Explanation: Outline refers to the outer edge or contour, which fits with something being visible "on the horizon." Craggy shapes accurately describes the rough, jagged appearance of mountains. The other options are less suitable: Colors; shapes – “colors” don’t “stand out as shapes.” Shapes; textures – “shapes” don’t stand out as “textures.” Textures; lines – “textures” don’t stand out as “lines.” So, "Outline; shapes" is the best fit both grammatically and contextually.

how should practicse these questions

questions.questionText: In the $1966$ Supreme Court decision Miranda v. Arizona, the court held that before the police can obtain statements from a person subjected to an interrogation, the person must be given a Miranda warning. This warning means that a person must be told that he or she has the right to remain silent during the police interrogation. Violation of this right means that any statement that the person makes is not admissible in a court hearing. This paragraph best supports the statement that : Police who do not warn persons of their Miranda rights are guilty of a crime. A Miranda warning must be given before a police interrogation can begin. The police may no longer interrogate persons suspected of a crime unless a lawyer is present. Persons who are interrogated by police should always remain silent until their lawyer comes.

questions.excerpt: Ramesh is wearing a new dress, isn't he? Wats wrong here?
questions.questionText: Ramesh is wearing a new dress, isn't he? Wats wrong here?
questions.questionHtml:
Ramesh is wearing a new dress, isn't he?

Wats wrong here?
questions.explanation: There are no errors in the statement: “Ramesh is wearing a new dress, isn't he?” Explanation:   The sentence is in the present continuous tense and is grammatically correct. "Ramesh" is the subject of the sentence, "is wearing" is the verb phrase in the present continuous tense, and "a new dress" is the direct object of the verb. The tag question at the end of the sentence uses the contraction "isn't he?" , which is a correct way to form a tag question in English. Also, the use of "isn't he?" at the end of the sentence is appropriate because the subject of the statement is singular ("Ramesh") and male, and "isn't he" is a common tag question used to confirm or seek agreement on a statement about a male subject.

questions.title: Work and Time
questions.excerpt: A is 20% less efficient than B. If B alone can do the work in 40 days then in how many days A and B can together complete the same work?The above question is from made ea...
questions.questionText: A is 20% less efficient than B. If B alone can do the work in 40 days then in how many days A and B can together complete the same work? The above question is from made easy test series. Sol: Given B alone can do the work in 40 days B’s one day work is 1/40 As A is 20% less efficient  So, A’s work one day work is  $\frac{1}{40}$x $\frac{80}{100}$ = $\frac{1}{50}$ So A alone can do the same work in 50 days.   A’s and B’s one day combined work =   $\frac{1}{40}$+ $\frac{1}{50}$ = $\frac{9}{200}$ Hence A and B together can complete the work in 22.22 days   My Doubt: Here A is 20% less efficient than B therefore   $\frac{Work \ done \ by\ B}{Work \ done \ by\ A}$= $\frac{100}{80}$ = $\frac{5}{4}$ But why it can’t be like  $\frac{Work \ done \ by\ B}{Work \ done \ by\ A}$= $\frac{120}{100}$ = $\frac{6}{5}$  as this also implies that A is 20% less efficient  Correct me if I am wrong. Is there a way to decide when to use which method?
questions.questionHtml:
A is 20% less efficient than B. If B alone can do the work in 40 days then in how many days A and B can together complete the same work?

The above question is from made easy test series.

Sol:

Given B alone can do the work in 40 days

B’s one day work is 1/40

As A is 20% less efficient 

So, A’s work one day work is $\frac{1}{40}$x $\frac{80}{100}$ = $\frac{1}{50}$

So A alone can do the same work in 50 days.

 

A’s and B’s one day combined work =  $\frac{1}{40}$+ $\frac{1}{50}$ = $\frac{9}{200}$

Hence A and B together can complete the work in 22.22 days

 

My Doubt:

Here A is 20% less efficient than B therefore  $\frac{Work \ done \ by\ B}{Work \ done \ by\ A}$= $\frac{100}{80}$ = $\frac{5}{4}$

But why it can’t be like $\frac{Work \ done \ by\ B}{Work \ done \ by\ A}$= $\frac{120}{100}$ = $\frac{6}{5}$ as this also implies that A is 20% less efficient 

Correct me if I am wrong.

Is there a way to decide when to use which method?

questions.questionHtml:
He was not only accused of theft ____________ of conspiracy.

  1. rather 
  2. but also
  3. but even
  4. rather than
questions.explanation: B. but also .... Not only … but also ... We use not only X but also Y in formal contexts: The war caused not only destruction and death but also generations of hatred between the two communities. The car not only is economical but also feels good to drive... This investigation is not only one that is continuing and worldwide but also one that we expect to continue for quite some time... We can sometimes leave out also: I identified with Denzel Washington not only as an actor but as a person. To add emphasis, we can use not only at the beginning of a clause. When we do this, we invert the subject and the verb: Not only was it raining all day at the wedding but also the band was late. Not only will they paint the outside of the house but also the inside. When there is no auxiliary verb or main verb be, we use do, does, did:  Not only did she forget my birthday, but she also didn’t even apologise for forgetting it.... 22 answered Feb 28, 2022 22 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please l

questions.excerpt: If the milkman doesn’t deliver milk or the geyser doesn’t work, then Akash will be late for school and lunch will be cooked late. Suppose lunch was actually cooked on tim...
questions.questionText: If the milkman doesn’t deliver milk or the geyser doesn’t work, then Akash will be late for school and lunch will be cooked late. Suppose lunch was actually cooked on time. Which of the following is definitely true? (a) Akash was late for school (b) Geyser worked (c) Akash reached school in time (d) Milkman did not deliver milk
questions.questionHtml:
If the milkman doesn’t deliver milk or the geyser doesn’t work, then Akash will be late for school and lunch will be cooked late. Suppose lunch was actually cooked on time.

Which of the following is definitely true?

(a) Akash was late for school

(b) Geyser worked

(c) Akash reached school in time

(d) Milkman did not deliver milk
questions.explanation: The answer should be B. Let P ≡ Milkman does not deliver milk, Q ≡ Geyser does not work, R ≡ Akash is late for school, S ≡ Lunch is cooked late. The statement is (P ⋁ Q) => (R ⋀ S) The contrapositive statement equivalent to this statement is ⌐(R ⋀ S) => ⌐(P ⋁ Q) ≡ ⌐R ⋁ ⌐S => ⌐P ⋀ ⌐Q Now since it is given Lunch is cooked on time hence ⌐S is true which makes the left hand side of the logic to be true. Hence this implies Both Milkman delivers milk and the Geyser works Thus option B is correct.

questions.questionText: Read the passage carefully and answer questions that follow: There is no doubt that the market as a reality and political economy as a theory played an important role in the liberal critique. But liberalism is neither the consequence nor the development of these; rather, the market played, in the liberal critique, the role of a “test, a locus of privileged experience where one can identify the effects of excessive governmentality and even weigh their significance; the analysis of the mechanisms of “dearth” or more generally, of the grain trade in the middle of the eighteenth century, was meant to show the point at which governing was always governing too much. Therefore, an analysis to make visible, in the form of evidence, the formation of the value and circulation of wealth – or, on the contrary, an analysis pre-supposing the intrinsic invisibility of the connection between individual profit-seeking and the growth of collective wealth-economics, in any case, shows a basic incompatibility between the optimal development of the economic process and maximisation of government procedures. It is by this, more than the play of ideas, the French or English economists broke away from mercantilism and commercialism; they freed reflection on economic practice from the hegemony of the “reason of state” and from the saturation of governmental intervention. By using it as a measure of “governing too much”, they placed it at the limit of governmental action. Liberalism does not derive from juridical thought any more than it does from an economic analysis. It is not the idea of a political society, but the result of search for a liberal technology of a government. Which of the following played a role in the liberal critique? Liberalism as a consequence of market forces Liberalism as an offshoot of political economy Reality of market Political economy as a practice

It is by this, more than the play of ideas, the French or English economists broke away from mercantilism and commercialism; they freed reflection on economic practice from the hegemony of the “reason of state” and from the saturation of governmental intervention. By using it as a measure of “governing too much”, they placed it at the limit of governmental action. Liberalism does not derive from juridical thought any more than it does from an economic analysis. It is not the idea of a political society, but the result of search for a liberal technology of a government.

questions.questionText: Read the passage and answer the question: Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in all kinds of organizational settings, whether industrial, educational, governmental, or military are attempting to run their organizations with the management by objectives process as a basic underlying management concept. Management by objectives is basically a process where by the seniors and the junior managers of an enterprise jointly identify its common goals, define each individual’s major areas of responsibility in terms of the results expected… use these measures as guides for operating the unit and assessing the contribution of each of its members. In some cases, this process has been successfully carria beyond the managerical level to include hourly employees. The concept rests in a philosophy of management that emphasizes an integration between external control by managers and self-control by employees. It can apply to any manager or individual no matter what level or function, and to any organization, regardless of size. The effective functioning of this system is an agreement between a manager and an employee about that employee’s groups performance goals during a stated time period. These goals can emphasise either output variables of intervening variables or some combination of both. The important thing is that goals are jointly established and agreed upon in advance. At the end of the time period, performance is reviewed in relation to accepted goals. Both the employee and the manager participate in this review. In an $\text{MBO,}$ organisation is managed through the identification of competing goals common objectives its specific characteristics senior and junior managers

The concept rests in a philosophy of management that emphasizes an integration between external control by managers and self-control by employees. questions.questionText: Bhaichung was observing the pattern of people entering and leaving a car service centre. There was a single window where customers were being served. He saw that people inevitably came out of the centre in the order that they went in. However, the time they spent inside seemed to vary a lot: some people came out in a matter of minutes while for others it took much longer. From this, what can conclude? The centre operators on a first-come-first-served basis, but with variable service times, depending on specific customer needs. Customers were served in an arbitrary order, since they took varying amounts of time for service completion in the centre. Since some people came out within a few minutes of entering the centre, the system is likely to operate on a last-come-first-served basis. Entering the centre early ensured that one would have shorter service times and most people attempted to do this.

questions.explanation: For the adjective 'little' - comparative is "less" and superlative is "least". "the more $\dots$ the less (room for error)" is correct usage Lesser means inferior, junior, subordinate etc. The adjective fewer is used to describe a countable noun and 'practice' cannot be counted. Hence, option C is the answer.

Look at this sequence $SCD\;\; TEF\;\; UGH \_\_\_\_WKL,$ and find the missing sequence.

  1. $CMN$
  2. $UJI$
  3. $VIJ$
  4. $IJT$
questions.explanation: The sequence is as follow: $S+1=T$ $T+1=U$ $U+1=V$  (the first alphabet is increment by 1from LHS side) $C+2=E$ $E+2=G$ $G+2=I$ (the second alphabet is increment by 2) $D+2=F$ $F+2=G$ $G+2=J$ (the third alphabet is increment by 2)   so the missing term is $VIJ.$ Hira Thakur answered Jan 22, 2019 • edited Nov 12, 2021 by Hira Thakur Hira Thakur comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.questionText: Check grammar and words , pls   I’ll talk about how maritime transport has been improved over the years. - We all know that sea is so large and the occurrence of accidents or ship crash are possible - So to ensure safety of ships, it has been developed some security systems  to track and communicate with ships using technology. - There are many useful systems, but I’ll only talk about two quickly - first one is what’s called : The Global Maritime Distress and Safety System - This system is the most famous marine system and most shipping companies use it - The idea of this system is to perform the following : 1- alerting : if a ship needs help for some urgent reasons , they can send a distress signal using a satellite 2- search : by using this system and GPS , they can locate ship’s position 3- rescue : and then rescue - This is a simple idea of this system - another system is what called ( Automatic identification system ) - It is an important system to avoid collision between ships and other objects. - the idea of this system that it can track ships location , their speed - and each ship use this system has a screen somewhere in the ship and it shows the other near ships that use the same system - also it has sensors to keep the ship away from other objects - these two systems could improve the maritime transport and safety. - of course , there are other useful systems   - but these are the most famous ones . - Now I’ll talk about the last point which is maritime transport in the future and how it would be. - the since has been improved and Scientists seek to improve what is called autonomous shipping - which is moving of ships from a port to other with no need of human help during the journey. - the idea of autonomous shipping is that it is not fully control self but the ship is controlling remotely from the port control station. - It is closed , covered and with a lot of cameras inside and outside - so we can say that autonomous shipping is shipping without crew and it is controlling remotely - the advantages of autonomous shipping are that it is safer , faster, and more efficient -  the main disadvantage is that is obvious that many sailors are going to lose their jobs. - and by the way first autonomous ship is going to seal next year in 2019.
questions.questionHtml:
Check grammar and words , pls

 

I’ll talk about how maritime transport has been improved over the years.

- We all know that sea is so large and the occurrence of accidents or ship crash are possible

- So to ensure safety of ships, it has been developed some security systems
 to track and communicate with ships using technology.

- There are many useful systems, but I’ll only talk about two quickly

- first one is what’s called : The Global Maritime Distress and Safety System

- This system is the most famous marine system and most shipping companies use it

- The idea of this system is to perform the following :
1- alerting : if a ship needs help for some urgent reasons , they can send a distress signal using a satellite
2- search : by using this system and GPS , they can locate ship’s position
3- rescue : and then rescue

- This is a simple idea of this system

- another system is what called ( Automatic identification system )

- It is an important system to avoid collision between ships and other objects.

- the idea of this system that it can track ships location , their speed

- and each ship use this system has a screen somewhere in the ship and it shows the other near ships that use the same system

- also it has sensors to keep the ship away from other objects

- these two systems could improve the maritime transport and safety.

- of course , there are other useful systems
 
- but these are the most famous ones .

- Now I’ll talk about the last point which is maritime transport in the future and how it would be.

- the since has been improved and Scientists seek to improve what is called autonomous shipping

- which is moving of ships from a port to other with no need of human help during the journey.

- the idea of autonomous shipping is that it is not fully control self
but the ship is controlling remotely from the port control station.

- It is closed , covered and with a lot of cameras inside and outside

- so we can say that autonomous shipping is shipping without crew and it is controlling remotely

- the advantages of autonomous shipping are that it is safer , faster, and more efficient

-  the main disadvantage is that is obvious that many sailors are going to lose their jobs.

- and by the way first autonomous ship is going to seal next year in 2019.

questions.title: What is the penalty for filling GST late?
questions.excerpt: A penalty of Rs.100 per day is applicable for late filling of GST return. The penalty would be payable for the period in which the taxpayer failed to furnish the return u...
questions.questionText: A penalty of Rs.100 per day is applicable for late filling of GST return. The penalty would be payable for the period in which the taxpayer failed to furnish the return up to maximum penalty of Rs.5000. If GST return for month is not filed, then the GST return for the next month cannot be filed by the taxpayer. Hence, late filling of GST return will have cascading effect leading to heavy fines and penalty.

questions.explanation: A can do the work in 10 days. B can do the work in 15 days. C can do the work in 20 days.   So, work done by A in one day = 1/10 Work done by B in one day = 1/15 Work done by C in one day = 1/20   So, work done by A and B together in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/15 = 10/60 Work done by B and C together in one day = 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60 Work done by A and C together in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/20 = 9/60   Now, to get max work in less days, A and B will work on 1st day, A and C on 2nd day ,and B and C on 3rd day.     Total work done in 3 days = 10/60 + 7/60 + 9/60 = 26/60 So, work done in 6 days = 52/60 Remaining work = 8/60 This can be done by A and B together.  They complete 10/60 Work in 1 day. So, they will take days for 8/60 Work = 60/10  × 8/60 = 4/5 days.   So,total number of days taken = 6 + 4/5 = 6(4/5) days.   Option C Gaurav Parashar answered Jul 11, 2018 Gaurav Parashar comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment.

Stalemate

A)Deadly

B)Dead-end

questions.explanation: The word stalemate is generally used in chess. Suppose A and B are playing chess. Now,assume A is not in check but cannot give any other move except into check. That is A cannot make progress in the game. This situation of A is called stalemate. This word is similar to the word deadlock. Deadlock means a situation where no progress can be made. So, option C will be the correct answer.

questions.explanation: This is basic of subject-verb agreement.  Here," as well as "  combine I and he to make( treat)  a single subject so that we use is instead of are. You can get various rule related to this in sub-verb agreement rule. Raj Kumar 7 answered Mar 18, 2018 Raj Kumar 7 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. 0 0 votes When two subjects are joined by as well as then you use verb according to the first subject. Here first subject is He which is singular and third person so you use 'is' instead of 'are'. Don't confuse it with just because there are two subjects you need a plural verb. There are some other words that have similar rule: along with, as well as, together with, except, besides, and not, like, unlike, etc. Rahul Ranjan 1 answered Mar 20, 2018 Rahul Ranjan 1 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.excerpt: Why should this absolutely God-given faculty of memory retain so much better the events of yesterday than those of last year, and, best of all, those of an hour ago? Why,...
questions.questionText: Why should this absolutely God-given faculty of memory retain so much better the events of yesterday than those of last year, and, best of all, those of an hour ago? Why, again, in old age should its grasp of childhood’s events seem firmest? Why should repeating an experience strengthen our recollection of it? Why should drugs, fevers, asphyxia, and excitement resuscitate things long since forgotten? . . . such peculiarities seem quite fantastic; and might, for aught we can see a priori, be the precise opposites of what they are. Evidently, then, the faculty does not exist absolutely, but works under conditions; and the quest of the conditions becomes the psychologist’s most interesting task. Which one of the following can be inferred from the passage? Psychologists are trying to understand how memory functions We tend to misunderstand our brains’ status quo. Psychologists believe that understanding the conditions under which the faculty of memory operates is the key to understand this faculty. The functions of faculty of memory are beyond human comprehension
questions.questionHtml:
Why should this absolutely God-given faculty of memory retain so much better the events of yesterday than those of last year, and, best of all, those of an hour ago? Why, again, in old age should its grasp of childhood’s events seem firmest? Why should repeating an experience strengthen our recollection of it? Why should drugs, fevers, asphyxia, and excitement resuscitate things long since forgotten? . . . such peculiarities seem quite fantastic; and might, for aught we can see a priori, be the precise opposites of what they are. Evidently, then, the faculty does not exist absolutely, but works under conditions; and the quest of the conditions becomes the psychologist’s most interesting task.

Which one of the following can be inferred from the passage?

  1. Psychologists are trying to understand how memory functions
  2. We tend to misunderstand our brains’ status quo.
  3. Psychologists believe that understanding the conditions under which the faculty of memory operates is the key to understand this faculty.
  4. The functions of faculty of memory are beyond human comprehension

options.label: A
options.text: Psychologists are trying to understand how memory functions

options.label: B
options.text: We tend to misunderstand our brains’ status quo.

options.label: C
options.text: Psychologists believe that understanding the conditions under which the faculty of memory operates is the key to understand this faculty.

options.label: D
options.text: The functions of faculty of memory are beyond human comprehension

questions.explanation: The correct option is C, which clearly follows from the last line of this passage.

questions.excerpt: If log 2 =0.30103, find the number of digits in 256  ?
questions.questionText: If log 2 =0.30103, find the number of digits in 2 56  ?
questions.questionHtml: If log 2 =0.30103, find the number of digits in 256  ?
questions.explanation: Result of log has two component integer part and decimal part, integer part is called characteristic and decimal part is called mantissa. Suppose log 2  = 0.30103, here 0 is characteristic and 30103 is mantissa. Now with the help of characteristic  we can find the number of digit in a given number. Like 2 is single digit number i.e (characteristic + 1) Similarly suppose we want to find number of digit in $2^{10}$ we can calculate it as log $2^{10}$ =  3.0103, Notice here characteristic part is 3, and number of digit will become (characteristic + 1) i.e 4, and $2^{10}$ i.e 1024 is actually 4 digit number. Similarly we can find number of digit in any cases with the help of characteristic. Now,number of digit in  $2^{56}$ will be log $2^{56}$ = 16.85168, here characteristic is 16, so number of digit will be 17. stblue answered Aug 13, 2017 • edited Aug 14, 2017 by stblue stblue comment Share Follow See all 16 Comments 16 16 Comments reply Show 13 previous comment

questions.title: why here in this we dividing by 2! plz tell detailed  explanation
questions.excerpt: There are 6 periods in each working day of a school. In how many ways can one organize 5 subjects such that each subject is allowed at least one period?sol :5 subjects ca...
questions.questionText: There are 6 periods in each working day of a school. In how many ways can one organize 5 subjects such that each subject is allowed at least one period? sol : 5 subjects can be arranged in 6 periods in  6 P 5  ways. Any of the 5 subjects can be organized in the remaining period ( 5 C 1  ways). Two subjects are alike in each of the arrangement. So we need to divide by 2! to avoid overcounting. Total number of arrangements = 6P5× 5C12!=1800= 6P5× 5C12!= 1800
questions.questionHtml:
There are 6 periods in each working day of a school. In how many ways can one organize 5 subjects such that each subject is allowed at least one period?

sol :

5 subjects can be arranged in 6 periods in 6P5 ways.

Any of the 5 subjects can be organized in the remaining period (5C1 ways).

Two subjects are alike in each of the arrangement. So we need to divide by 2! to avoid overcounting.

Total number of arrangements
= 6P5× 5C12!=1800= 6P5× 5C12!= 1800

questions.questionHtml:
thief bahgu ram is spotted by the policeman pakkad singh from a distance of 200 m.once they see each other

start running .what id the distance bahgu ram whose running at 5kmph would have covered before being caught

by pakad singh running at 7 kmph?
questions.explanation: In this question let's assume that the thief is caught after time T after being spotted by the policeman Now in this time 'T' let's suppose the thief covers X meters . Since the policeman was 200 meters behind the thief, he needs to cover 200+X meters in this time 'T' . Therefore we get the following equation: X/5=200+X/7 on solving this equation we get X=500 meters asriv answered Jun 2, 2017 asriv comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.explanation: At first it is saying that the amount is doubled after 6 years compounded annually(by default). therfore :  $2P = P\left ( 1+ \frac{R}{100}\right)^{6}$ Now the maturity amount means the mone earned is again deposited for next 36 years more ( 42 years from the start) Hence we get  $A = 2P\left( \left ( 1+ \frac{R}{100}\right)^{6}\right)^{6}$  $A = 2P\left (2 \right)^{6}$  $A = 2P \ast 64$ Here 2P will be the amount deposited now and it will be 64 times after those many years. questions.explanation: Answer should be Off . No one gonna say take your shoes on when you enter the room. If we use with then it sounds incomplete sentence . Most possible answer should be Off shekhar chauhan answered Jun 8, 2016 shekhar chauhan comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. 2 2 votes To take off , when used in this context, is a separable phrasal verb.  This means that if it's used with a noun or noun-phrase, such as "your shoes" the noun or noun-phrase can go either in the middle of the phrasal verb or at the end as in this question. so option C should be correct. but It's important to note that  to take off  is not always separable. When used in the context of aircraft or business it is inseparable: "The plane took off" "Business is really taking off this year".

questions.excerpt: Moving into a world of big data will require us to change our thinking about the merits of exactitude. To apply the conventional mindset of measurement to the digital, co...
questions.questionText: Moving into a world of big data will require us to change our thinking about the merits of exactitude. To apply the conventional mindset of measurement to the digital, connected world of the twenty-first century is to miss a crucial point. As mentioned earlier, the obsession with exactness is an artefact of the information-deprived analog era. When data was sparse, every data point was critical, and thus great care was taken to avoid letting any point bias the analysis. From “BIG DATA” Viktor Mayer-Schonberger and Kenneth Cukier. The main point of the paragraph is: The twenty-first century is a digital world Big data is obsessed with exactness Exactitude is not critical in dealing with big data Sparse data leads to a bias in the analysis
questions.questionHtml:
Moving into a world of big data will require us to change our thinking about the merits of exactitude. To apply the conventional mindset of measurement to the digital, connected world of the twenty-first century is to miss a crucial point. As mentioned earlier, the obsession with exactness is an artefact of the information-deprived analog era. When data was sparse, every data point was critical, and thus great care was taken to avoid letting any point bias the analysis. From “BIG DATA” Viktor Mayer-Schonberger and Kenneth Cukier. The main point of the paragraph is:

  1. The twenty-first century is a digital world
  2. Big data is obsessed with exactness
  3. Exactitude is not critical in dealing with big data
  4. Sparse data leads to a bias in the analysis

questions.excerpt: Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order, he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite tem...
questions.questionText: Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order, he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite temperament. He was guilty of throwing away his wicket several time after working hard to lay a strong foundation. His critics pointed out that until he addressed his problem, success at the highest level will continue to elude him.  Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above passage? He was already a successful batsman at the highest level. He was to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman. He failed to make many of his good starts count. Improving his technical skills will guarantee success. iii and iv ii and iii i, ii and iii ii only
questions.questionHtml:
Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order, he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite temperament. He was guilty of throwing away his wicket several time after working hard to lay a strong foundation. His critics pointed out that until he addressed his problem, success at the highest level will continue to elude him. 

Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above passage?

  1. He was already a successful batsman at the highest level.
  2. He was to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman.
  3. He failed to make many of his good starts count.
  4. Improving his technical skills will guarantee success.
  1. iii and iv
  2. ii and iii
  3. i, ii and iii
  4. ii only

questions.title: GATE CSE 2015 Set 3 | Question: GA-6
questions.excerpt: Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia.Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above senten...
questions.questionText: Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia. Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentence? Alexander would not have turned his attention towards India had he not conquered Persia. Alexander was not ready to rest on his laurels, and wanted to march to India. Alexander was not completely in control of his army and could command it to move towards India. Since Alexander's kingdom extended to Indian borders after the conquest of Persia, he was keen to move further.
questions.questionHtml:
Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia.

  1. Students should come at $9.00$ a.m. and parents should come at $10.00$ a.m.
